test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 24 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The curved surface area of a cylinder is 484 sq. cm. If height of the cylinder is 7 cm, then what is the volume of the cylinder (in cubic cm)? (Use π = (22)/(7))
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Curved Surface Area (CSA)** = 2πrh = 484 cm²

**Volume** = πr²h = (2πrh × r) ÷ 2

First find radius: 2 × (22/7) × r × 7 = 484 ⇒ 44r = 484 ⇒ r = 11 cm

Volume = (CSA × r) ÷ 2 = (484 × 11) ÷ 2 = 242 × 11 = 2662 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 2662 cm³.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Curved Surface Area (CSA)** = 484 cm²

**Height (h)** = 7 cm

**Formula Used:**

CSA of cylinder = 2πrh

Volume of cylinder = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7d2fc70acca6342a6c3471b58fcd91cbdce38750e85f7436828a4e2a77c5c015.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r × 7 = 484

⇒ 44 × r = 484

⇒ r = 484 ÷ 44 = 11 cm

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 11² × 7

⇒ Volume = 22 × 121

⇒ Volume = 2662 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 2662 cm³.**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

The **Total Surface Area (TSA)** includes the curved area and two circular bases: TSA = 2πr(h + r).

Hollow Cylinder Volume

For a cylinder with outer radius R and inner radius r: Volume = π(R² − r²)h.

Relation between Volume and CSA

The volume of a cylinder is directly proportional to the radius when CSA is fixed: Volume = (CSA × r) ÷ 2.</p
